scope: six original DEV topics; twelve draft answers and six T finals; each arm denominator90, not full-exam60
exposure: Aggregate 7 versus 4.5 and 14 versus 4 errors; first T007 draft/final accidentally visible. Remaining drafts anonymized. No owner per-item grades read.
word_count_method: Strip leading topic heading; count whitespace-separated tokens containing a Unicode letter/digit. Standalone punctuation is not a word.

items.label: R01
argument_evidence: Political: magnate/local power after administrative disruption is a causal argument, despite generality.
Economic: plunder destroys workshops/crops, reducing trade and fiscal rebuilding capacity.
Social: mortality, hunger, epidemic and displacement are linked to damaged settlement and religious distrust.
factual_errors: P2: permanent loss of Pomerania is materially misleading; Royal Prussia was retained. Scope ambiguous because Lębork/Bytów changed status in1657.
uncertainties: Mass deportation scale/attribution is unsupported precision; not a second established error.
Centralized in magnate hands means local oligarchic concentration, not necessarily a logical contradiction.

items.label: R02
argument_evidence: Political: prestige and recognition repeated without a concrete diplomatic act or coronation; superficial.
Church: Gniezno1000 and independent hierarchy explicitly support administrative cohesion.
Military: Czech and Kyiv expansion linked to strategic territory, force and prestige.
uncertainties: Lubuszy may be garbled Łużyce; counted as ambiguous terminology rather than established invented conquest.
Monarch equal to emperor overstates aspiration but is not a claimed formal legal rank.
No automatic penalty for omitting coronation from this draft.

items.label: R03
argument_evidence: Military: Warsaw1920 and Niemen successes explain survival and defensive capacity.
Political: defeating revolution and Riga connect sovereignty to time for institution building.
Territorial: Belarus/Ukraine and eastern urban centres explain strategic/economic scope.
factual_errors: P2: general Piłsudski is the wrong1920 rank; he was Marshal.
uncertainties: Wilno was not awarded by Riga; the essay attributes its security to the war broadly, so this is an imprecise linkage rather than a second certain error.
Bolshevik military power finally broken is rhetoric about this campaign, not literal permanent Soviet disarmament.

items.label: R04
argument_evidence: Constitutional: veto blocks fiscal/military reform and weakens defence; causal process supports thesis.
Internal: magnate clientelism connects private interests with fragmented collective action.
International: named powers/rulers, intervention and correctly dated partitions support external pressure.
factual_errors: P2: inability to establish permanent defence taxes contradicts the1717 settlement. Treat tax/standing-army absence as one fiscal-military misconception.
uncertainties: Modern army wording may mean inadequacy rather than literal absence.
Frederick II is not expressly said to have personally conducted all three partitions; do not invent that error.
Failure of appropriate reform is a one-sided interpretation, not proof the author denies every reform.

items.label: R05
argument_evidence: Constitutional: veto/fiscal weakness explains inability to modernize.
Internal: patronage and factional dependence explain external manipulation.
International: neighbours, interference and three correct partition dates explain final destruction.
uncertainties: Strong fiscal/military institutions absent is imprecise but not the same as denying any standing taxes/army.
No canon checklist: absence of a named confederation alone does not erase the explained clientelist mechanism.

items.label: R06
argument_evidence: Territorial: key treaty settlement is mostly wrong, leaving a weak correct northern-gains core.
Political: prestige/subordination core remains but supposed foundation and lasting peace distort the mechanism.
Economic: exports, access and merchant markets form a relevant causal chain.
factual_errors: P1: Pereśwaga is not an identifiable battle in these wars; unsupported invented battle.
P2:1466 transfer of Samogitia to Poland is wrong in territory, recipient and settlement.
P2:1466 Polish acquisition of parts of Masuria is wrong.
P3:1466 created the Prussian Order state is wrong; that state pre-existed the treaty.
P3: conflict definitively ended and regional relations stayed stable for centuries is false; later Polish-Teutonic war1519–1521 is a counterexample.
uncertainties: The last error is sensitive to rhetorical rather than literal reading; count range4–5.
Territorial and political lower argument levels reflect loss of usable supporting facts, distinct from the single rubric error deduction.

items.label: R07
argument_evidence: Political: expansion/prestige mechanism has little reliable concrete support and invented successor.
Church: independent hierarchy effect is relevant but central event is invented.
Military: general annexation/integration claim rests on a wrong dated example; Lusatia is the limited valid core.
factual_errors: P2: alleged successor Władysław I Badêmy is invented; successor was Mieszko II.
P3: council at Mogiła in1000 is wrong; Gniezno meeting/metropolis.
P4: capture of Prague in995 is wrong; Chrobry took Bohemia in1003.
uncertainties: Silesian campaigns may conflate Mieszko I and Chrobry, but vague undated wording is not counted as a fourth error.
Gniezno bishopric wording lacks archiepiscopal precision but is not counted separately from the ecclesiastical-event error.

items.label: R08
argument_evidence: Territorial: Grunwald1410, Warmia and1466 gains linked to security; sufficient despite omitting Gdańsk by name.
Political: repeated prestige/arbitration/safety assertions without explaining treaty dependency; superficial.
Economic: access to ports, grain/timber exports and trade growth connect gains to prosperity.
factual_errors: P3: elimination of the Order as a future military threat is overstated as a settled fact; later wars refute literal reading.
uncertainties: Grunwald broke military power means severe defeat rather than immediate state extinction.
Trade monopoly language is broad and weakly supported; not treated as a separate established legal monopoly claim.
Error count0–1 depending on rhetorical reading; politics remains shallow either way.

items.label: R09
argument_evidence: Political: weakened crown, magnate power and multi-front pressure explain reduced international capacity.
Economic: destruction of urban/agrarian production explains fiscal impoverishment and slow recovery.
Social: war/epidemic mortality and regional depopulation explain lasting social disruption.
uncertainties: Factories and total war are loose modern wording, not automatically a distinct historical falsehood.
Russian/Brandenburg pressure is placed in the broader concurrent-war context; no invented specific territorial settlement.
No quantified demographic claim to test.

items.label: R10
argument_evidence: Political: unnamed underground activity and organic work give only a general account of preserving political identity.
Cultural: teaching, press and reading groups explain intergenerational language transmission.
Social: cooperatives/professional/agricultural associations link economic self-help to durable national organization.
uncertainties: Geography across partitions is insufficiently differentiated, but the Russian repression statement is explicitly scoped to Russia.
Malformed sentence in political paragraph does not break the recoverable overall argument.

items.label: R11
argument_evidence: Political: unnamed liberal/national organizations and1905 protests give a thin political account.
Cultural: literature/press explain historical memory and language survival, despite a disputed parenthesis.
Social: reading associations/church/teaching explain cross-class solidarity.
factual_errors: P3: generalized ban on Polish-language books overstates censorship; legal Polish publication continued.
uncertainties: First pass additionally counted Sienkiewicz later period and Towarzystwo Czytelników. Both are now non-counted ambiguities: later can mean later nineteenth century; the malformed organization name can be recognizable imprecision.
The church-as-refuge claim is broad, not a specific false legal assertion.
items.adjudication: Two ambiguous allegations removed after conservative semantic/source check; first pass preserved.

items.label: R12
argument_evidence: Military: Warsaw manoeuvre and mobilization explain survival.
Political: Riga/sovereignty argument remains usable despite wrong attribution of federalism.
Territorial: eastern border/Belarus/Ukraine and strategic hinterland are functional, with a contradictory safety conclusion.
factual_errors: P2: Piłsudski is incorrectly styled general in1920.
P3: the defeated federal conception is assigned to the Bolsheviks instead of Piłsudski.
P4: the Riga border supposedly removed direct Soviet adjacency; Poland still bordered Soviet territory.
uncertainties: Coherence2: the eastern-border paragraph jumps from setting a border with the opponent to removing that adjacency. This is the identified internal inference defect, not an automatic extra factual-error penalty.
If coherence judged separately as intact, high bound restores that point.

finals.argument_evidence: Retains the earlier territorial/economic argument and shallow political repetition. Adds a new false Grunwald-result partition into Prussian/Livonian states; no score gain.
uncertainties: New Grunwald-caused Prussian/Livonian division is an error.
Earlier eliminated-future-threat allegation retained, with rhetorical uncertainty.
Samogitia loss after1410 is simplified but temporary cession in1411 makes it not a separate certain error.

finals.argument_evidence: Political evidence now names coronation1025 and Bautzen1018. Church argument adds independent dioceses and Adalbert. Military evidence specifies Moravia/Kyiv/Red Ruthenia and strategic effects. Satisfactory across all three; rich military/church interpretation is possible.
uncertainties: Moravia1003 conventional chronology has scholarly dating uncertainty; no invented precise contradiction established.
Status equal to emperor remains inflated rhetoric.

finals.argument_evidence: Targowica1792 and named leaders now concretely illustrate rollback and external dependence. Fiscal error remains. Conclusion says no modern reforms while body describes reforms being dismantled: minor unsupported/contradictory conclusion, coherence2.
uncertainties: Do not count the French diplomatic break as invented merely because unfamiliar; historical accounts describe it.
Frederick II context does not explicitly assign him1793/1795.
No rich score merely from adding names.

finals.argument_evidence: Pomerania allegation removed; economic/social causal chains retained. Warsaw90% is a published estimate, not independently established precision. No automatic reward just for adding a number.
uncertainties: Warsaw90% varies with geographical population definition/period; not a secure falsehood.

finals.argument_evidence: Military paragraph adds Wieprz/Komarów/Niemen; removes the wrong general rank. Sovereignty and territory arguments remain functional. Wilno remains broad war attribution, not explicitly a Riga award.
uncertainties: Scope of Wilno/Riga linkage still deserves qualification.
Extra battle list alone does not force rich argument credit.

finals.argument_evidence: Political paragraph gains a concrete1905 concessions/organization mechanism; culture/social chains retained. Gains are tempered by a1906 party inserted into a period ending1905.
uncertainties: PPS Revolutionary Faction dates to1906, outside the specified endpoint.
Legal unions also require1906 qualification; cluster treated as one out-of-scope revolution-aftermath issue; two-error count leaves deduction unchanged.
Return of Polish to schools applies especially to private institutions; general wording is imprecise.

limitations: No owner per-item grades read, even after first-pass freeze.
Factual counts are reviewer claim classifications, not objective validated benchmark labels. Some central allegations remain interpretation-sensitive; exact14-to4 is not robustly reproduced.
General causal historical processes can earn satisfactory credit without a prescribed proper-name checklist. No essay automatically gains coherence for headings or loses it for repetition.
No training/retrieval writes, model calls, May2025 access, Git or remote mutation.
